svg.title: Flee, and Glorify God in Your Body
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 5 panels. Panel 1 (1 Corinthians 6:12-13): two men of Corinth talking in a city street. Caption: "Corinth: what some were saying." A Corinthian says: "All things are lawful for me". Another Corinthian says: "Food is meant for the stomach and the stomach for food". Note: "The quotation marks are the ESV’s reading: Paul quotes them." Panel 2 (1 Corinthians 6:13): Paul standing in a room, holding a scroll. Caption: "Paul answers." Paul says: "The body is not meant for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body." Panel 3 (1 Corinthians 6:19-20): three empty crosses on a rise at dusk; a believer in white stands looking up at them. Caption: "The reason: you were bought." Paul says: "You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body." Note: "The price: “the precious blood of Christ” (1 Peter 1:18-19)." Panel 4 (Genesis 39:12; 1 Corinthians 6:18): Potiphar's wife, a rich Egyptian woman in white linen with a gold collar, holds Joseph's garment; Joseph runs for the doorway. Caption: "Joseph left his garment in her hand and fled." Paul says: "Flee from sexual immorality." Note: "His reason, settled before: “sin against God” (Genesis 39:9)." Panel 5 (1 Corinthians 6:11): three believers in white robes standing in morning light, arms raised. Caption: "And such were some of you." Paul says: "But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified". The point: Your body is the Lord’s: He bought it, He will raise it, and it is joined to Him. So flee, and glorify God in your body (1 Corinthians 6:13-20).
svg.text: FLEE, AND GLORIFY GOD IN YOUR BODY
Sin and sexual immorality in one minute
Your body is the Lord’s: He bought it, He will raise it, and it is joined
to Him. So flee, and glorify God in your body (1 Corinthians 6:13-20).
Potiphar’s wife is unnamed in Scripture; her Egyptian dress is drawn from the period, not the text.
